sources.section: Form 1120-S page 1 income/deductions; Schedule K line 1
sources.text: Author paraphrase: ordinary trade/business income is reported on page 1 line 22 and Schedule K line 1, excluding portfolio income and separately stated deductions. This restricted fixture uses receipts less returns, cost of goods sold, deductible rent, documented business supplies, and booked W-2 officer wages. Cash draws/distributions are not operating deductions. Assume no other book-tax differences.

Author paraphrase: taxable portfolio bank interest is separately stated on Schedule K line 4 / K-1 box 4, not ordinary operating income. Qualifying cash charitable contributions are separately stated on Schedule K line 12a / K-1 box 12, not page 1 operating deductions. Non-dividend cash distributions are reported for the actual recipient, not treated as wages or an operating expense. All fixture donations have the required receipt/acknowledgment, involve qualifying cash gifts, and no corporate-level tax or accumulated C-Corp earnings apply.

sources.section: Schedule K-1 item G and box 1
sources.text: Author paraphrase: absent ownership changes, allocate ordinary income/loss by each shareholder's percentage held throughout the year. Ownership changes generally require daily allocation and additional facts. Report ordinary loss on the K-1 before shareholder-level basis, at-risk and passive limitations. Distributions belong to their actual recipients and do not determine ordinary-income allocation.

Author paraphrase: shareholder-employees performing services must receive reasonable compensation before non-wage distributions. Reasonableness depends on facts such as duties, time, experience and comparable pay. The IRS may reclassify distributions as wages. This guidance supplies no automatic salary percentage; do not invent a salary or claim that any positive wage is adequate.

sources.section: Limitations on losses, deductions and credits
sources.text: Author paraphrase: losses/deductions at shareholder level can be limited by stock/debt basis, at-risk rules, passive activity rules and excess business loss limits, in that order. Form 7203 generally supports basis calculations. A negative K-1 amount does not by itself establish the amount deductible on a shareholder return.
